::: {#exm-racket-level-order}
#### Level order in Racket

The level order (@def-level-order) needs a queue (@def-queue).
Here the queue holds subtrees rather than vertices:
removing a subtree that is not empty lists its root and adds its two subtrees at the back,
and removing an empty tree adds nothing.

```racket
(define (level-loop queue)
  (if (empty? queue)
      empty
      (let ([T (first queue)])
        (if (empty? T)
            (level-loop (rest queue))
            (cons (first T)
                  (level-loop (append (rest queue)
                                      (list (second T) (third T)))))))))

(define (level-order T)
  (level-loop (list T)))
```

- `(let ([name value]) body)` gives `name` the value `value`, and then returns the value of `body`.
  Here it names the front of the queue `T`.
- `(append xs ys)` is the list of the elements of `xs` followed by those of `ys`,
  so the two subtrees go to the back of the queue.

With `B` as in @exr-racket-tree, `(level-order B)` returns `'(m f t c h r w j p)`, the level order of @exm-level-order.
Each subtree that is not empty enters the queue when its parent's subtree is removed,
just as `bfs` marks a child when it removes the parent.

:::
